cold_open.hook: AMD crashed 7.9% while the Booker Prize just crowned 13 novels nobody's read yet—two different kinds of AI hype, same day.

markets.macro_note: Tech selling pressure offset by enterprise software strength; VIX creeping up on rate uncertainty.

big_story.story_title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) Surged on an Agentic AI-Driven Server CPU Renaissance
big_story.angle: AMD's agentic AI server play was supposed to be the narrative that saved the stock—instead it tanked 7.9% today, exposing how thin the conviction is on who actually wins the next chip cycle.

quick_hits.angle: UPS raised full-year guidance but admits domestic Q3 revenue will be flat—the logistics company is saying 'we're doing great, but also nothing's moving.'
JetBlue's Q2 loss widened as fuel costs surged 81%—airlines are now just fuel hedges with wings attached.
Kevin Warsh's Fed press conference will be revealing even without a rate hike—the real signal is what he *doesn't* say about inflation.
Cursor's India push with localized pricing ahead of SpaceX acquisition is a bet that AI coding tools need geographic arbitrage to scale—or it's just cheap labor optics.

odd_thing.joke_angle: The Booker Prize longlist just dropped 13 'dynamite' novels—which is exactly how many people will actually read them before the winner is announced.

yesterday_callback.topic: AMD just tanked 7.5% while Adobe soared 5.5%—the AI trade is officially splitting into winners and wreckage.
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: AMD tanked *harder* today at -7.9%, proving yesterday's split wasn't a blip—it's the actual structure of the AI trade: infrastructure plays are collapsing while enterprise software (Accenture +6.6%) keeps climbing.
